narration.text: GPS clocks gain 38 microseconds a day from relativity.
Without correction, positions would drift quickly.
The system became fully operational in 1993.
If it went dark, phones would lean on cell towers and Wi-Fi.
But networks and markets that use GPS timing would feel it too.
So GPS isn't just maps. It's the world's shared clock.
